## Greater emphasis on payment performance can help merchants capture lost revenue and retain customers


Software companies help merchants grow by building tools that attract customers, streamline operations, create better experiences and drive more sales. Payments have become part of that value proposition. What was once considered a back-office function is now embedded directly into software experiences.


But as digital commerce has matured, a new challenge has emerged. Many businesses are still losing revenue after a customer has already decided to buy.


The problem isn’t demand. The problem is payment performance.


Failed transactions, outdated card credentials, fraud-related friction and avoidable declines can quietly chip away at revenue. Most of these losses happen behind the scenes, making them difficult for businesses to identify and even harder to measure.


The hidden cost of payment failure


Consider a subscription business. A customer may be perfectly satisfied with a service and intend to stay for years. But if the card on file has expired or been replaced, the next billing attempt may fail. The customer often doesn’t realize what happened.


The merchant assumes the customer churned. In reality, the relationship was disrupted by outdated payment credentials.


As transaction volumes grow, these seemingly small disruptions can become significant sources of revenue leakage. For software platforms looking to create more value for merchants, payment optimization is becoming an increasingly important part of the conversation.


The goal of payment optimization is simple: Ensure more legitimate transactions are approved, completed and retained.


Crystal Tran


VP, Product Strategy & Value-Added Services, Fiserv


What is payment optimization?


At its core, payment optimization is the practice of maximizing payment performance across the customer lifecycle. It combines strategies and technologies designed to reduce avoidable payment failures, improve authorization outcomes, minimize friction and help merchants capture more of the revenue they’ve already earned.


Why payment performance now matters even more


The rise of recurring and online commerce has fundamentally changed the payments environment. For subscription businesses, marketplaces and software platforms, payment success is no longer measured by a single transaction. It is measured by the ability to sustain revenue and customer relationships over months and years.


What trends are making payment optimization increasingly important?


First, online transactions have a higher risk of fraud than in-person ones,


with hackers and scammers tapping new technologies to disrupt them.


Second, consumers frequently replace payment cards


because of expirations, fraud events, lost cards and account updates. This creates challenges for businesses that rely on stored payment credentials.


Third, businesses face growing pressure to do more with existing customers.


Customer acquisition costs continue to rise across many industries, increasing the importance of retaining every dollar of revenue already earned.


With these factors in mind, payment performance is more than an operational metric; it is a revenue and customer retention strategy.


From payment processing to payment optimization


Leading software platforms are expanding their focus beyond payment acceptance to help merchants integrate payments and maximize successful transactions. There is no one-size-fits-all approach. The right strategy depends on a business’s payment mix, customer behavior, recurring billing models, risk profile and growth objectives.


The process begins by examining questions such as:


- How many legitimate transactions are being declined?


- How often are recurring payments failing because of outdated credentials?


- Where is payment friction impacting customer experience?


- How can fraud be reduced without creating unnecessary barriers for legitimate buyers?


As they answer these questions, more businesses are adopting a layered approach to payment performance. Rather than relying on a single tool, they are combining capabilities, such as network tokenization and card account updater services that help keep payment credentials current, reduce unnecessary declines, strengthen fraud defenses and improve transaction success rates.


This layered strategy results in more efficient payment processing and creates a more resilient payment ecosystem that supports revenue growth and customer retention.


Payment optimization creates ongoing advantages for both software companies and the merchants they serve.


Crystal Tran


VP, Product Strategy & Value-Added Services, Fiserv


Benefits for everyone


For merchants:


- More successful transactions


- Reduced payment interruptions


- Stronger recurring revenue performance


- Better customer experiences


- Lower operational burden


For software companies:


- Increased platform value


- Stronger merchant retention


- Reduced payment-related friction


- Improved merchant outcomes


- Greater competitive differentiation


Your strategic takeaway


Businesses invest significant resources to acquire and retain customers. Payment optimization supports these investments and keeps customer relationships intact by protecting them from expired cards, outdated account information, avoidable declines and unnecessary friction. In this way, it serves as both a technical safeguard and a direct driver of customer retention.


When software companies can help merchants capture what might otherwise be lost, payments become a strategic business advantage.
